[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested simple exercises to help with posture and back pain, including:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Shoulder blade squeeze: Sit or stand with arms by sides, squeeze shoulder blades together, hold for a few seconds, repeat 10 to 15 times.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Cat-cow stretch: Start on all fours, inhale and arch back (cow pose), exhale and curve spine (cat pose), repeat 10 to 15 times.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Seated twist: Sit cross-legged, twist upper body to the right, hold for a few seconds, repeat on the other side, do 5 to 10 times each side.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Hip flexor stretch: Kneel on right knee, stretch left hip flexor, hold for a few seconds, switch sides, do 5 to 10 times each side.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Wall angels: Stand against a wall, raise arms with elbows, wrists, and backs of hands touching the wall, slide arms up and down, repeat 10 to 15 times.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended performing the exercises daily to see improvement in posture and back pain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised to listen to the body and adjust the intensity or duration of exercises as needed, and to consult a healthcare professional if experiencing pain or discomfort.
